newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asiatrust sees more lending to Filipino-Chinese.
newsitem.headline: Asiatrust sees more lending to Filipino-Chinese.

text.p: Asiatrust Bank, due to be listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange next week, foresees a 50 percent growth in its loan availments to domestic Chinese small and medium enterprises (SME), bank officials said on Tuesday.

"The main factors are the booming economy and the fact that we are generating new accounts, mostly Chinese businesses," said Joseph Chua, assistant vice president of the bank, which has Chinese lending units (CLUs) devoted to servicing Chinese SMEs.

He said 50 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio of 3.55 billion pesos for fiscal year ending June 1996 went to the high growth Chinese SME sector. Loan portfolion for fiscal year 1995 totalled 3.04 billion pesos.
Majority of Asiatrust Bank is owned by Filipinos with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Singapore-based Asean Strategic Capital Ltd being part owners, Chua said.
Shirley Benedicto, head of Asiatrust's CLUs, said lending to small businsses was a challenge.

"Typically, the Chinese shy away from borrowings unless it is intended to fund expansion projects or to acquire fixed assets. Ordinarily, they would want their operations to be funded mainly by recurring income."
